USA.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Keep the July 6 List 1 tariffs in place and let the statutory comment process on List 2 and the proposed $200B List 3 run, but do not implement the next tranche yet. Reopen talks now and insist on enforceable IP and tech-transfer remedies, not another purchase-only communiqué. Use the unused $200B list as leverage at the table, and let the already-announced farm relief absorb harvest-season pressure so we are not forced into a panicked concession or a consumer-facing tariff cascade.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: The threat to US interests is real but still contained. The March 22 Section 301 finding established a genuine structural problem—forced tech transfer and IP theft—and China has now matched the first $34B tranche with 25% duties on soybeans, autos, aircraft and other politically sensitive US exports (timeline 2018-07-06; Politico 2018-07-06). Soy is a concentrated exposure (~$12–14B, a large share of US bean exports), futures have already dropped hard, and USDA’s July 24 authorization of up to $12B in Market Facilitation and related aid is an official admission that retaliation is biting agriculture. That maps above neutral on the USA threat scale. It does not map to +0.5: industrial production is still rising (INDPRO 103.36 in July), Michigan sentiment is only slightly off (97.9), VIX closed 12.29 on July 25, and goods imports from China actually jumped to $47.0B in July on front-loading—so the real-economy drag is sectoral, not systemic. The May 19 joint statement (China to “significantly increase” purchases; Mnuchin calling the war “on hold”) then collapsed on May 29, proving a purchase pledge without structural commitments is not a settlement. Escalating List 3 now would move the fight onto consumer goods, invite non-tariff Chinese counters (inspections, licensing delays) once Beijing runs out of US goods to tax, and lock in Brazilian soy substitution. The ZTE denial-order lift (July 13) already spent a major non-tariff chip. With List 3 published but not in force, unused leverage still exists; the disciplined use of it is to negotiate from the current posture rather than fire the next round or roll back.
key_factors: List 1 ($34B at 25%) is live and China matched it the same day, targeting soy, autos, and aircraft
US farm-belt exposure is concentrated and already priced in; USDA authorized up to $12B in relief on July 24
US macro still healthy: rising IP, low VIX, only a mild dip in sentiment — no material GDP shock yet
May 19 purchase-only truce collapsed within 10 days; structural IP/tech-transfer issues remain unaddressed
Proposed $200B List 3 is in comment and is unused leverage; imposing it now would hit US consumers and invite non-tariff retaliation
ZTE ban already lifted (July 13), so a major non-tariff chip has been spent
CNY depreciation (~6.33 to 6.77) and China’s smaller import base show Beijing is under pressure but not collapsing

sources_cited.excerpt: USTR Section 301 report finds China's IP/tech-transfer practices unreasonable; Trump directs tariffs, a WTO case, and investment restrictions.
US and China joint statement: China agrees to significantly increase purchases; Mnuchin says trade war is on hold.
White House announces the US will proceed with Section 301 actions including 25% tariffs on ~$50B; truce collapses.
List 1 tariffs take effect: US 25% on ~$34B of Chinese goods; China imposes matching ~$34B retaliation the same day.
USTR publishes proposed List 3: ~$200B of Chinese imports for an additional 10% tariff; public comment begins.
US industrial production still rising: latest 103.36 (2018-07-01), +1.63% over the window.
VIX 12.29 on 2018-07-25 — equity vol is calm, not pricing a systemic shock.
US goods imports from China jumped to $47.0B in July 2018 from $39.0B in February — front-loading, not collapse.
CNY weakened from ~6.33 in late January to 6.7658 on 2018-07-25 (~6.8%), a pressure signal on China.
Nearly one-third of US soybeans (~$14B) go to China; 25% Chinese tariff incentivizes Brazilian substitution and has already cut expected soybean profitability by nearly $100/acre.
USDA authorizes up to $12B in programs, in line with an estimated $11B impact of retaliatory tariffs on US agricultural goods.
Commerce lifted the ZTE denial order on July 13 after a $1B penalty, $400M escrow, leadership overhaul, and 10-year compliance monitors.
List 3 would hit consumer products; China bought only ~$135B of US goods last year and is expected to retaliate with inspections and administrative delays once goods-tariff room runs out.

CHN.rationale:
RECOMMENDATION: Keep the existing dollar-for-dollar July 6 retaliation in place and do not fire a new tariff or non-tariff package against the still-proposed $200B list. Reopen a quiet high-level channel to test whether Washington will pause List 2/List 3 in exchange for a talks process, without repeating the May purchase-only offer that the White House discarded ten days later. Continue the WTO cases and the public multilateralism line; treat any further U.S. implementation as the trigger for a calibrated response, not a reason to pre-escalate now.

SUPPORTING RATIONALE: Threat is material but not yet at the high/existential CHN anchors. List 1 is already live at 25% on ~$34B and is aimed at aerospace, ICT, robotics and other Made-in-China-2025 lines (timeline 2018-06-15, 2018-07-06); Trump has directed a further ~$200B at 10% if we retaliate and USTR published that list on July 10, so the export base and industrial-policy agenda are clearly in the crosshairs. The ZTE denial order of April 16 showed the U.S. can freeze a national champion overnight; even though Commerce lifted the ban on July 13 after a $1.4B package, board purge and a 10-year suspended denial order, the tool remains on the table. FX pressure is real: CNY/USD moved from the mid-6.3s in the spring to 6.7658 on July 25 (~7% weaker), Trump has accused Beijing of currency manipulation, and a disorderly slide would revive 2015-style outflow risk even though PBOC has said it will not weaponize the yuan. That combination sits below +0.5 because List 3 is still in a comment/hearing process (written comments due mid-August), industrial production is still running about +6% YoY, reserves are roughly stable near $3.14T, and U.S. goods imports from China were still rising into July (front-loading, not a collapse). Action should stay at hold/negotiate rather than escalate: we already matched $34B, U.S. goods exports to China are far smaller than $200B so another tariff volley cannot be symmetric and would give Washington a pretext to lock in List 3 and threaten a further $200B, and the May 19 joint statement (China to “significantly increase” purchases; Mnuchin said the war was “on hold”) collapsed on May 29—so conceding purchases again, without a U.S. standstill, would spend leverage for nothing. Negotiate without new commitments preserves optionality through the List 3 comment window, keeps the WTO track (MOFCOM filed against the $200B proposal on July 16), and leaves room to retaliate later if the 10% list is actually imposed.
key_factors: List 1 ($34B at 25%) already in force and aimed at MIC2025 sectors
Proposed List 3 (~$200B at 10%) not yet imposed; comment process runs into August
Asymmetric goods trade: China cannot match $200B with tariffs and a preemptive volley risks locking in List 3
Yuan down ~7% since spring; FX/stability risk, not a controlled export subsidy
ZTE denial order demonstrated entity-list vulnerability but was lifted 13 July on costly terms
May purchase-deal truce collapsed within 10 days; do not re-offer purchases unilaterally
China real economy not yet breaking: IP ~+6% YoY, reserves ~$3.14T

sources_cited.excerpt: List 1 tariffs take effect: US 25% on ~$34B of Chinese goods. China imposes matching ~$34B retaliation the same day.
USTR publishes proposed List 3: ~$200B of Chinese imports for an additional 10% tariff (~6,000 product lines). Public comment / hearing process begins.
Trump directs USTR to identify an additional ~$200B of Chinese imports for 10% tariffs if China retaliates against the $50B action.
US and China release joint statement after talks: China agrees to "significantly increase" purchases of US goods and services. Mnuchin says trade war is "on hold."
White House announces the US will proceed with Section 301 actions, including 25% tariffs on ~$50B of Chinese imports. Truce collapses.
US Commerce Department bans ZTE from buying US components (denial order). ZTE faces operational shutdown. Major non-tariff escalation.
CNY per USD 6.7658 on 2018-07-25 versus ~6.33 in late January / mid-6.2s–6.3s in March–April; about +6.8% on the dollar over the window.
China industrial production still +6.0% YoY as of 2018-07-01, only a mild deceleration from 107.2 in February.
China reserves ex-gold about $3.14T in July 2018, down only ~0.5% over the window — no reserve crisis.
Commerce lifted the ZTE ban on 13 July after ZTE paid $1B, placed $400M in escrow, overhauled leadership, and accepted a 10-year U.S. compliance monitor / suspended denial order.
China announced a WTO challenge to the proposed $200B list; MOFCOM called U.S. actions slander and said Washington is fully responsible for the escalating war.
In response to USTR’s $200B list, China indicated it was considering non-tariff retaliatory measures; List 3 comments/hearings run through mid-to-late August.
PBOC said the yuan slide reflected market expectations, not intended guidance, and that China would not use the exchange rate as a tool in the trade conflict.
